summary: LoCoMo is a tight ten-conversation benchmark that stress-tests whether an LLM agent can actually recall and reason over very long-term dialogue, with clean QA and event-summarization annotations plus RAG-style observation and session-summary databases you can regenerate locally. For something like Proreerfolio, where the whole point is grounding a résumé in a person's accumulated project history rather than letting a model confabulate, this is a practical way to measure whether my retrieval layer is pulling the right evidence instead of the most recent token. The synthetic-conversation generator with assigned personas is also a neat trick for stress-testing agent memory in PenguPool without needing real user histories, and the fact that the whole eval loop is a handful of bash scripts calling OpenAI, Anthropic, or HuggingFace endpoints keeps it small enough to run on a laptop before I trust it in a pipeline.
